nodes.label: DSA Learning Hub
nodes.author: Amandeep Singh Khanna
nodes.rationale: Interactive educational website for searching and sorting algorithms, built for the Computing for Data Science Lab course at St. Joseph's University.

nodes.label: Binary Search
nodes.rationale: Requires sorted input; halves the search space each step, giving O(log n) instead of Linear Search's O(n).

nodes.label: Data Structures and Algorithms
nodes.rationale: Framed as a CS foundation that need not be intimidating; taught via analogies, visualisers, and annotated Python rather than lectures.

nodes.label: Linear Search
nodes.rationale: Must return -1 when the target is missing. Poor choice for large sorted data that is searched repeatedly; Binary Search is then far more efficient.

nodes.label: Quick Sort
nodes.rationale: Not stable; Python uses Timsort for sorted() because it is a stable O(n log n) sort. Quick Sort is used where average-case speed and low extra memory matter (C qsort, databases). Last-element pivots on sorted input yield O(n²); partition rearranges while quick_sort only recurses.

nodes.label: Stack
nodes.rationale: LIFO used for browser history, language call stacks, undo/redo, parentheses matching, and DFS. Recursion in Quick Sort is implemented via the call stack.

nodes.label: Dark/Light Mode
nodes.rationale: Theme preference is persisted in localStorage so the choice survives reloads.

nodes.label: Brain Map
nodes.rationale: Pedagogical pattern: explain how to code each topic as numbered reasoning steps before showing annotated Python.

nodes.label: Divide and Conquer
nodes.rationale: Break a problem into smaller identical sub-problems, solve trivial pieces, then combine. Teaching analogy: Russian nesting dolls for recursion.

nodes.label: Vanilla HTML CSS JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Zero dependencies and no build step: open index.html in any modern browser. Trade-off is a single-page teaching site rather than a framework app.
